# Test fixtures

Sample PDFs that the tests open. All are generated by `make_fixtures.py`:

```
python tests/fixtures/make_fixtures.py
```

The PDFs are committed to git. Running the script again gives byte-identical
files, so git only shows a fixture as changed when the script changed. (One
exception, explained below: `encrypted_user_pw.pdf`.) When you change the
script, update the facts below too.

All positions are in PDF points in PyMuPDF's convention: origin at the
top-left of the *unrotated* page, y grows downward, 1 point = 1/72 inch.
Every page is US Letter (612 × 792 points) with 12 pt Helvetica text.

## simple_text.pdf

- 2 pages, no rotation.
- Page index 0:
  - "Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet." with its baseline starting at (72, 90).
    `search_for("Lorem")` returns about `Rect(72, 77, 106, 94)`.
  - "The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog." with its baseline starting
    at (72, 120).
- Page index 1:
  - "This is the second page." with its baseline starting at (72, 90).

## rotated_pages.pdf

- 4 pages, rotated 0°, 90°, 180° and 270° (page index × 90).
- Each page has one line, "Rotation 0" / "Rotation 90" / "Rotation 180" /
  "Rotation 270", with its baseline starting at (72, 90) in unrotated
  coordinates.
- `page.mediabox` is 612 × 792 on every page.
- `page.rect` is 612 × 792 on the 0° and 180° pages and 792 × 612 on the 90°
  and 270° pages.
- The unrotated point (72, 90) is displayed at (72, 90), (702, 72),
  (540, 702) and (90, 540) on the four pages.

## cropbox_offset.pdf

- 2 pages whose visible area (CropBox) is `Rect(30, 40, 582, 762)` on the
  paper, so `page.cropbox_position` is (30, 40).
- Page index 0 is not rotated: `page.rect` is `Rect(0, 0, 552, 722)`.
- Page index 1 is rotated 90°: `page.rect` is `Rect(0, 0, 722, 552)`.
- Each page has the line "Cropped page", written with its baseline at
  (72, 90) on the paper. Measured from the visible area's corner, as
  PyMuPDF does, the baseline starts at (42, 50).

## page_labels.pdf

- 8 pages with the page labels i, ii, iii, iv, 1, 2, 3, 4 (roman numerals
  for the first four pages, then digits starting again at 1).
- Each page has the line "Page index N" (N = 0 to 7) at (72, 90).
- So the page labelled "3" is page index 6, and the third page is labelled
  "iii". No page is labelled "5".

## not_a_pdf.pdf

- Not a PDF at all: the 24 bytes `This is not a PDF file.` plus a line break.
- `pymupdf.open()` raises `FileDataError`; `DocumentModel.open()` raises
  `PdfOpenError`.

## broken_xref.pdf

- A copy of `simple_text.pdf` in which the number after the final
  `startxref` (the position of the object table) was replaced by `99999`,
  which lies beyond the end of the file.
- It still opens: MuPDF rebuilds the table. `doc.is_repaired` is True, there
  are 2 pages, and the text is the same as in `simple_text.pdf`.

## encrypted_user_pw.pdf

- 1 page with the line "This page is password protected." at (72, 90).
- Encrypted with AES-256. User password: `test`. Owner password: `owner`.
  (Public on purpose: they protect nothing.)
- **Only written when the file is missing.** Encryption uses fresh random
  numbers on every save, so this file can never be byte-identical twice.
  To regenerate it, delete it and run the script.

## ../../src/pdfeditor/resources/self_test.pdf

- Not a test fixture but generated by the same script: the PDF the app
  opens for `python -m pdfeditor --self-test`. It lives inside the package
  so the packaged app carries it along.
- 1 page: "PDF Editor self-test" at (72, 90) and "If you can read this,
  opening and drawing a PDF works." at (72, 120).
